topic: R14: Anthropic surfaces per scenario (Messages API, tool use, Batches, Managed Agents, Agent SDK, Skills, memory) for MYEZ live compares, KB growth, critique loops and operator tooling
summary: Answer to the owner: no, MYEZ does not need agents, sessions or Skills for any of its seven scenarios. Every row is either one model call or a pipeline our own code drives. Recommended default: (1) the live path (compare, coming-soon classifier, photo ID) uses the plain Messages API with structured outputs (output_config.format) and prompt caching on a frozen system prompt and tool list, streaming, with Haiku 5.5 as the worker and Sonnet 5.5 only for the verdict or a low-confidence photo. (2) Nightly jobs (critique re-grading, normalising enrichment and PDP refreshes) go through Message Batches: 50% off every token, cache reads included, results within 24 h. (3) Scheduling stays on our own Railway cron services, which the repo already uses (scripts/cron_*.py, railway.warmer.json). Managed Agents scheduled deployments would work mechanically: cron, up to 9 min of jitter, dollar budgets, run records. But they lose the batch discount, are beta, keep state on Anthropic's side, and run web_fetch and sandbox egress on Anthropic's infrastructure. That last point means our fail-closed robots.txt ruling and the Cloudflare stop rule could not be enforced by our own fetcher. (4) Operator tooling: Claude Code or the Agent SDK on the owner's machine, with narrow dedicated tools and writes gated behind approval. Agent Skills (they need the code-execution container; code execution is not ZDR-eligible) and the memory tool or memory stores have no role on the live path, and none elsewhere: the knowledge base must be our own queryable Postgres, not files hosted by Anthropic. Task budgets (minimum 20,000 tokens) suit only agent loops; we have none. Cost shape: web search at $10 per 1,000 searches outweighs Haiku 5.5 tokens ($0.10/$0.50 per MTok) about 10 to 1 on a typical compare (computed, not measured), so knowledge-base-first plus a max_uses cap is the main cost lever. Changes since session 80: there is still no Anthropic adapter or pin at 95cf6f86. The docs give the Sonnet 5.5 cache read as $0.10, not the skill's $0.20, and Files storage as 1 TB, not 100 GB. Haiku 5.5 thinks by default and has no server-side fallback. Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 return 400 on any non-default temperature, which breaks the temperature=0 the verdict relies on for determinism (model_config.py:107-123).

findings.claim: Owner question answered: none of the seven scenarios meets the skill's agent criteria. Each is a single call or a pipeline our code orchestrates. 'Agents' in Managed Agents are versioned configs plus sessions, and nothing here needs Anthropic to run the loop or host a workspace. The live path is Messages API only. Nightly work is Batches plus our own cron. Operator work is local Claude Code or the Agent SDK.

findings.claim: Row (a) live compare under the 30 s cap. Surface: Messages API, streaming, server-side web_search with max_uses 2-3, allowed_domains set to the merchant registry and user_location BH. Haiku 5.5 at effort low/medium does extraction and Sonnet 5.5 at effort medium does the verdict, both via output_config.format; no forced tool_choice. Caching: one breakpoint on the frozen system prompt and tools (512-token minimum), 5-minute TTL, or 1 h if traffic gaps run longer. Cost: about $0.0013 for 8K in / 1K out on Haiku, versus $0.01 per search; the Sonnet verdict is about $0.03 at 8K/1.5K. Latency: first-request schema compile (then a 24 h schema cache), the search pause, possible pause_turn. Credentials: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var on Railway (name only). Needs no hosted state.

findings.claim: Managed Agents scheduled deployments, measured from the skill. POSIX cron with an IANA timezone; execution jittered up to 15% of the interval (minimum 5 s, maximum 9 min); 1,000 deployments per org; a dollar budget is copied onto each fired session. A rate-limited firing is recorded with no retry, missed triggers are not backfilled, and archiving the agent archives the deployment. Pricing adds $0.08 per session-hour, and the Batch API discount does not apply to sessions.

findings.claim: Row (f) nightly critique and eval re-grading. A Message Batch over the day's compares, with Sonnet 5.5 as judge at effort medium and a structured rubric output. Server-side fallbacks are rejected inside batches, so refusals are retried per custom_id. Managed Agents outcomes (a grader that iterates one deliverable) are unnecessary. The repo already has a nightly eval cron.

findings.claim: Web search facts. Versions are 20250305, 20260209 (dynamic filtering) and 20260318 (response_inclusion). Errors come back as HTTP 200 with error_code values: too_many_requests, invalid_tool_input, max_uses_exceeded, query_too_long, request_too_large, unavailable. On an error, content is an object, not a list. Failed searches are not billed. encrypted_content must be passed back unchanged, and citations are always on.

findings.claim: Pitfalls from the skill. (1) Haiku 5.5 thinks by default; thinking disabled is allowed only at effort high or below; responses can start with thinking blocks, so read content by type; thinking text is omitted by default. (2) Sonnet 5.5 rejects thinking disabled with a 400 and uses between_tools instead (effort high or below, no other fields). (3) Forced tool_choice any/tool returns 400 on Sonnet 5.5, Batches included; Haiku 5.5 accepts it but then skips thinking. (4) Prefill returns 400 on both. (5) max_tokens defaults: about 16000 non-streaming, about 64000 streaming, about 256-1024 for classification. (6) Server-tool errors do not raise. (7) Fallbacks: Sonnet 5.5 accepts only fallbacks 'default' (beta server-side-fallback-2026-07-01, Claude API only); Haiku 5.5 has no server-side fallback (a list returns 400); fallbacks are rejected in Batches.

recommendations: Use the plain Messages API with output_config.format and a cached frozen system+tools prefix for rows (a)-(c). Reason: single-shot calls with no hosted state, and the skill's 'start simple' rule.

Gate non-fragrance requests deterministically at $0 before any model call, and only send ambiguous text to Haiku 5.5 (effort low, enum output, max_tokens about 1024). Reason: meets the zero-cost refusal requirement, and thinking counts toward max_tokens.
Cap web_search with max_uses 2-3 and allowed_domains drawn from the merchant registry, and check the KB first. Reason: at $10 per 1,000 searches, search costs roughly 10x a Haiku compare's tokens.
Move ENABLE_SELF_CRITIQUE work off the live path into a nightly Message Batch on Sonnet 5.5. Reason: 50% cheaper and removes a model call from the 25 s stream cap.

Run PDP refreshes and enrichment normalisation as Batches submitted by a new Railway cron (pattern: scripts/cron_eval_nightly.py, railway.warmer.json), with a 1 h cache TTL. Reason: batch discount, plus our own fetcher keeps robots fail-closed and the Cloudflare stop.

Do not adopt Managed Agents deployments for (e)/(f) now. Reason: no batch discount, beta, Anthropic-hosted state, and web_fetch/egress on Anthropic's servers outside our politeness rules. Revisit only if a genuinely open-ended discovery agent is needed.
Set blocked_domains for Fragrantica and Parfumo on every web_search/web_fetch tool definition. Reason: the standing ban must also hold when search runs on Anthropic's servers.

Handle stop_reason refusal and max_tokens before parsing, branch on the web_search_tool_result content type (list vs error object), and abstain rather than fabricate. Reason: server-tool errors do not raise, Haiku 5.5 has no server-side fallback, and the no-fabricated-numbers rule applies.
Use fallbacks 'default' only on Sonnet 5.5 calls on the Claude API, never on Haiku 5.5 and never in Batches. Reason: a fallback list returns 400 on Haiku 5.5, and fallbacks are rejected in batches.
Re-run the verdict-determinism A/B before switching providers. Reason: temperature=0 (model_config.py:107-123) returns 400 on Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5.

Before writing the adapter spec, verify Haiku 5.5 web search support via Models API capabilities.server_tools.web_search. Reason: the skill and the docs disagree on which web_search versions Haiku 5.5 accepts.
Use Claude Code or the Agent SDK locally for operator data fixes, with gated write tools and local env credentials. Reason: no service-role key stored with Anthropic, and the repo is public.
